Run complete. Summary for Bill:

**LBY progress filler â€” 57/57 gaps searched, zero nils, 125 files staged and undelivered.**

Gap list was 57 of the 121-indicator frame (64 held going in). No prior LBY run, so nothing was skipped as a prior nil. Five parallel slices, 114 Exa Agent briefs, 530 candidates returned, 182 fetched, 33 dropped.

**137 selections over 125 distinct files** after the Â§4a cap â€” **55 baseline, 70 progress**. Those two counts are what to decide between if the week tightens; the batch is splittable by a folder move. Every one of the 57 indicators has staged evidence.

- **Merge**: three duplicate-URL groups collapsed, four files withdrawn (MICS7 findings report, the LyGIF roadmap, one LANA post), `full` kept over `excerpt`, baseline-wins applied, every selected row repointed and nothing decremented. Each survivor's note carries what the withdrawn capture knew.
- **One instrument staged twice by design**: CBL circular 18/2025 from the Central Bank's own PDF and from lawsociety.ly â€” different indicators, different hosts, date conflict recorded rather than settled. Six further `published` disagreements recorded in place.
- **`lint-staged-queue.py` clean over both folders, nothing withdrawn as misfiled.** All 125 also checked mechanically: notes round-trip through YAML, date prefixes padded and equal to `published`, `places`/`sweep_batch`/`topics` all correct, every body's `URL:` line matches its frontmatter.
- **28 origin adjudications** â€” 27 watch, one drop (`lawhub.info` serves Egyptian legislation unlabelled by jurisdiction, inside a Libyan legal search). Note 109 is `[ACT]` and asks OSINT to append them.
- **The route finding worth reading**: `lana.gov.ly` answers HTTP 200 with its own homepage for the wrong `lang`, never a 404. A sweep trusting the status code stages the front page as an article body. It is in note 109.
- Acted on OSINT's new note 17 in passing: retagged a CIDCAâ€“CMAâ€“WMO MoU from `geopol.china` to `finance.mou`.

Share committed and pushed as two commits â€” OSINT's 139-file BFA hand-carry as OSINT's, this batch as Corpus's. Corpus registers committed and pushed.

**What it consumed, against Â§7's four stages.** Stage 1, the sweep: one session, **1h 18m**, five concurrent slices, ~2.44M sub-agent tokens and 861 tool calls. Stage 2, OSINT's ingest of the 125 files: not this session's cost but the same weekly pool â€” on note 17's figures (BEN 150 and BFA 139 across fourteen Phase A slices) that is roughly seven ingest slices. Stage 3, the mapping pass: one working Corpus session, and the expensive half â€” 125 bodies read against 57 indicator rows; costs OSINT nothing. Stage 4, render: minutes inside a normal render. Yield is 57 probed with evidence staged for all 57; gaps actually *closed* is not knowable until stage 3.

**Two things you need to do.** The batch sits in `new-queue\LBY\baseline\` (55) and `new-queue\LBY\progress\` (70) and is **not queued for ingest until you move it**. And `logs/progress-report-log.csv` is still open in Excel (PID 3700) â€” LBY's `Filler Searched` cell could not be written, retried across the run. I was at the five-block cap in `messages-for-bill.md`, so rather than write a sixth I amended the existing block: it now names DZA, EGY and LBY, lines 24â€“26, fifth column, `03/09/2026`.
